summary: Closing an issue withdraws every open ask of the issue (asks.issue_key = key, state open) with a new server-only resolution kind `withdrawn` naming the closer, writes the blocks' state (and their copies') into the live documents before closed_at is set, and runs a final owner-verified sweep after SetIssueClosed so no block reads open; reopening restores exactly the withdrawn asks and writes their blocks back to open, so no version is cut; an idempotent repair pass at boot and every 10 minutes withdraws asks left open on closed issues (attributed to the latest issue.closed actor, dated at the pass) and restores withdrawn asks on open issues; the SPA card on a closed issue's current document shows the row's record; contracts add `withdrawn` and read `legion-daemon:<PROJECT>` whole.

findings.finding: F1: live writes on closed issues meet closed-owner and closed-room guards; warm/cold path dependence.
findings.answer: Decision 4: close, reopen and repair hold the issue row and run their document writes owner-verified (withOwnerVerified, honoured by allowInject docs/websocket.go:351-373); the close's in-transaction writes precede the status UPDATE; ordinary edits/answers/resolutions keep 409 ISSUE_CLOSED. Task 2 tests a resident room flagged closed and a non-resident document.

findings.finding: F2: Docs.Join requires the ledger commit protocol and lock order; no settlement wait under locks; multi-issue repair locking.
findings.answer: Decision 7: Docs.Join, deferred Discard, ledger.Commit before SetIssueClosed (still WithoutCancel). Decision 5: pre-close settlement runs with no transaction or lock. Lock order in Risks; the repair runs one transaction per issue under its row.

findings.finding: F3: event order and last_seq in the PATCH response; daemon reads LastSeq through GET.
findings.answer: Decision 6 and Task 3: LockOwners before the first append, document writes before events, ask events before the status event, after loaded once ask and ledger events are in; test compares response last_seq with GET and expected_sequence success/ISSUE_CHANGED.

findings.finding: F4: unindexed blocks in the settle window get no record; state-only marking incomplete.
findings.answer: Decision 5: synchronous pre-close settlement indexes them so the close withdraws them with a record; a final owner-verified sweep after SetIssueClosed marks any block settlement did not index (failure, concurrent edit) state=resolved, which a reopen's settlement indexes as an open ask with its author. Tests with a 1-hour settle delay, a failing settlement hook and a browser edit after the fork.

findings.finding: F5: copy classification: answered-source copies, same-id unrelated blocks, live-only copies, earlier-wording rule.
findings.answer: Decision 2: only own blocks and blocks copiedAskSources classifies as copies of the withdrawn asks, classified over the live fork before the rows change; answered/resolved-source copies and unrelated blocks untouched; Task 2 tests each.

findings.finding: F6: no-version claim unsupported; spec requires earlier versions unchanged, not no later version.
findings.answer: Decision 3: stored versions never rewritten (version hashes tested); a fully settled document writes no version across close+reopen; real pending text is versioned by the existing protocol (pre-close settlement).

findings.finding: F7: lifecycle writes credit the closer/reopener as pending authors.
findings.answer: Decision 9: credited like resolveAsk/answerAsk credit their block-state writes; existing pending authors never cleared.

findings.finding: F8: approval carry reads rows; restored approval requests must keep version, requested_version, hand-back and turn; no review from the close.
findings.answer: Decision 8: withdrawal writes only the resolution; reopen sets only state/resolution; tests assert no ask.answered/artifact.approved/changes_requested/review rows and the restored request's id, approval, requested_version and waiting_on.

findings.finding: F9: rolling deploy and boot-pass failure policy.
findings.answer: Decision 10: the repair runs at boot and every 10 minutes, both directions, per-issue transaction re-reading under the issue row; tests for two concurrent runs, idempotence and restore direction.
Decision 10: actor of the latest issue.closed event with all its fields; an issue with none is logged and skipped.

findings.finding: F11: version view must not show a later withdrawal.
findings.answer: Decision 12: the record shows only on a closed issue's current document (ProofDocument); VersionView keeps reading its own attributes; browser spec checks a saved version.
Decision 11: actor-label reads a session id beginning legion-daemon: whole; INFRA-73's closing actor read from production is exactly {kind:session,id:legion-daemon:INFRA}.

findings.finding: F13: older-client compatibility claim too broad.
findings.answer: Decision 14: old close callers valid; envoy-client falls back to the raw payload; an SPA bundle loaded before the deploy needs a reload.
Plan's acceptance matrix maps each acceptance clause to its check and surface (Go API, Playwright on the real Go server, branch CLI on dispatch:local, production check).
